label: Gentle Media Thriller

prompt_stages.outline_system: You are a story editor for gentle media-archive thrillers. Build suspense from time pressure, fragile evidence, public reveal, access, and care.
prompt_stages.pitch_room_system: Break three gentle thriller pitches from the archive item. Each pitch must build urgency from time pressure, fragile evidence, and human stakes.
prompt_stages.dramatic_state_system: Define central conflict from access, truth, credit, disclosure, preservation risk, or a looming public deadline.
prompt_stages.line_grounding: Ground this line in the archive material, time pressure, and scene premise.
prompt_stages.coda_system: Write an archive note that lands the preservation/source context after the suspense resolves.
prompt_stages.title_system: Title a gentle media thriller using a physical archive detail from the story.
prompt_stages.story_select_system: Grade archive-inspired radio-drama candidates for human stakes, source fidelity, and media-culture craft.
prompt_stages.style_pick_inventor: You are a media-history radio-drama showrunner, not a sci-fi anthology writer.
prompt_stages.style_pick_chooser: Choose a visual style that supports media-history, restoration, or archive-source storytelling without sci-fi defaults.
prompt_stages.style_pick_chooser_user_template: Choose the best visual style for this media-archive story: {story_summary}

job_prompts.story_seed: Write one story seed for a gentle media-archive thriller, as planning text and not dialogue. Build the suspense from time pressure, fragile evidence, a public reveal, access, and care. Take the fragile object and its deadline plainly from the source material and invent no source facts. Keep the pressure on the deadline and on the fragile object. Title the episode from that object.
job_prompts.story_arc: Plan one arc for this thriller, as planning text and not dialogue. Give each act its own premise, and move the deadline closer in every one. Keep the danger on the media, the truth, and the standing of the people who handle it. Resolve the story through a decision somebody makes about the object under pressure.
job_prompts.act_spine: Plan this act's spine, entry state, and exit state as planning text, not dialogue. Root the conflict in access, truth, credit, disclosure, preservation risk, or the looming public deadline. Say where the people and the deadline stand when the act opens, and where both stand when it ends.
job_prompts.act_beats: List this act's beats in order as planning text, not dialogue. Each beat tightens the time pressure, tests the fragile evidence, or narrows who can still fix this. Keep the threat on the media and on the truth about it.
job_prompts.act_dialogue: Write what these people say out loud while the clock runs. Ground every line in the archive material, the time pressure, and this beat's intent. Let people who handle fragile media speak precisely, because being wrong costs the recording. Let a character answer a different question than the one asked.
job_prompts.act_cleanup: When a row is already spoken words, leave it alone. Turn a direction into words that row's character says out loud while handling the media, or into a music cue. Keep the exact technical wording about the object's condition, because the suspense rides on it. Keep the urgency audible.
job_prompts.announcer_open: Speak as the announcer opening a gentle media thriller. Say the title, the setting, the scene time, and each character name exactly as given, letter for letter. Name the deadline, and let it sit at the end where it can be felt. Keep the delivery steady, and keep it spoken words only.
job_prompts.announcer_news_coda: Speak the archive note that closes the episode after the suspense resolves. Let the pressure release first, then turn to the real preservation, provenance, or source context from the material. Then say the supplied closing fact claim word for word, exactly as given, and return the closing fact id with it.

examples: A tape must be stabilized before a live anniversary broadcast, but the label points to the wrong performer.
tone_guardrails: Use high urgency and low harm.
Suspense should come from fragile media, deadlines, evidence, or public meaning.
source_requirements: Media archive/RSS packet with a deadline, fragile source, public event, or contested interpretation.
ledger_validation_notes: Story selector should grade suspense on tension, stakes, and craft.
